top.title: Knicks put Karl-Anthony Towns trade on the table as $276 million extension talks stall
top.description: Photo by Caleb Bowlin/Getty Images The New York Knicks have reportedly put a potential Karl-Anthony Towns trade on the table as negotiations over a lucrative contract extension continue to stall. Towns is eligible to sign a four-year extension worth approximately $276 million, but the Knicks are facing financial restrictions under an alleged mandate from owner James Dolan to avoid entering the second luxury tax apron. The 30-year-old still has two years remaining on his current contract, although the final season is a player option that could allow him to become an unrestricted free agent in 2027. New York Knicks could consider trading Karl-Anthony Towns if extension talks fail According to Sean Deveney of Heavy on Sports , New York has discussed the possibility of trading Towns if he decides his future lies away from the franchise. Deveney explained that the Knicks have made the option clear to the centre as both sides continue to work towards an agreement. “The Knicks would be crazy to trade Towns at this point, but then, the Knicks are crazy not to have found common ground on an extension before the season started,” Deveney wrote. “So, we can’t rule out a deal if it looks like Towns will seriously weigh leaving in the summer of 2027. The Knicks have put that option on the table for him, and he will have suitors if nothing changes between now and June 30.” However, the financial gap between the two sides remains significant. According to Stefan Bondy of The New York Post , Towns turned down a four-year offer worth approximately $200 million during the summer. That figure was around $77 million below the maximum extension available to him and would also have represented a pay cut from his current $57 million salary. The Knicks may also have to consider the contracts of Josh Hart and Jalen Brunson, who are both eligible for extensions at different points. Towns’ expectations could also have been influenced by Jalen Duren’s new four-year, $200 million extension with the Detroit Pistons. An anonymous executive told SNY’s Ian Begley that New York would likely need to offer Towns more than Duren received, given his experience and standing in the league. With Towns potentially able to test free agency in 2027, the Knicks face an important decision over whether to meet his financial demands or explore a trade before his contract situation becomes more complicated. top.title: Providence's offense hits early warning signs in loss to Nebraska
top.description: UNCASVILLE, Conn. – Mohegan Sun Arena looked like Friartown West . The energy was high. The defensive effort fit the blueprint. But it’s hard to win a game shooting 31 percent. Providence did enough to make life difficult on Big Ten contender Nebraska but couldn’t make life easy on itself in a 67-58 defeat Saturday night in the Hall of Fame Tip-Off. “What an amazing crowd. The Friar fanbase did their job tonight. But we did not,” Providence head coach Bryan Hodgson said. “Quite frankly, we’re not good enough yet to win that caliber of basketball game. But I can tell you this: we will be.” Nebraska withstood a burst of energy from the Friars and their crowd in the opening minutes. Both teams struggled to score for much of the first half, but the Cornhuskers slowly started to exert their will, then delivered a 9-0 run to jump in front by 11. Providence made a late charge before halftime and trailed by five at the break. The uphill battle included foul trouble for projected standout Miles Byrd, who sat much of the first half with two, then picked up two more in the opening minutes of the second half. The Friars made a move to get within three points with 13:31 left, but the Huskers rolled from there, out-scoring Providence 22-9 over the next 11 minutes. Leonardo Marangon led the Friars with 12 points. Making his debut after a preseason injury, Devin Vanterpool had 11 points and six rebounds. Nebraska’s Pryce Sandfort led all scorers with 25 points. Providence continued to find mixed results at Mohegan Sun Arena despite the proximity to campus, falling to 5-7 all-time. Here are three takeaways from the matchup. Offensive woes too much to overcome The numbers said it all for the Friars at the offensive end: 31 percent from the field, 18 percent from 3-point range, 18 turnovers. Nebraska used some matchup zone, and the Friars never looked comfortable against it. At times, they executed for open looks but couldn’t get them to fall. Other trips looked disjointed. “Offensively, we were in a massive rut,” Hodgson said. “Can’t win a game when you have 10 assists and 18 turnovers, shoot 18 percent from 3.” The 3-point shooting was especially troublesome, given the volume of shots the Friars took. Thirty-eight of their 62 field-goal attempts were from beyond the arc, and they made only seven. The obvious about the offensive struggles: was it just a bad night against a good team or will it be a trend? “They’re about as disciplined a defensive team as I’ve faced in my coaching career,” Hodgson said. “I didn’t put our guys in a good enough position offensively to win that game, and we’ll get that fixed.” Defense and effort are something to build on The Friars plan to make defense their calling card this season, and they look capable of doing so. Nebraska won despite shooting 45 percent from the field and making just five of 24 from beyond the arc. Providence forced 15 turnovers and out-rebounded the Huskers 33-31. top.title: Rapid Reaction: Northwestern falls to Iowa 24-10 in aggravating defeat
top.description: Northwestern fans knew missing Aidan Chiles would hurt. It was unclear exactly how much. Chiles brought athleticism and talent that was one of a kind in college football. In his place tonight was backup quarterback Nicco Marchiol following a reported upper-body injury to Chiles that occurred in the Oregon game. This game was something that could be described as an offensive meltdown. The offense couldn’t move the ball — part of the reason why the game finished 24-10. Without mastermind Aidan Chiles at the helm, the offensive unit looked stuck. Giving up 24 points to the Hawkeyes isn’t terrible, considering just how dominant they were last week against Wisconsin, but the defense was still having trouble stopping the run and explosive plays, though they did cause a few turnovers that momentarily swung some momentum toward the ‘Cats. Then special teams gave up a touchdown. As far as the score went, it was relatively competitive in the first half. However, the game never really looked or felt competitive. Nicco Marchiol went 24-for-32 passing for 181 yards and a touchdown totaling the same amount of rushing yards as both of the two primary backs combined at 52-yards, with Himon at 27-yards and Komolafe at 25-yards. TE Luke Dehnicke had a great night also considering Marchiol’s primary passing method on the night was short dump off passes to either WR Hayden Eligon or one of the running backs. Dehnicke had five catches for 52 yards and WR Griffin Wilde also (ironically) had five catches for 52 yards. Iowa started off the game explosive from their own 25-yard line, crossing midfield in just two plays with completions to both Reece Vander Zee and Tony Diaz. The Hawkeyes continued pushing the drive from the pocket with a completion to Vander Zee down to the NU 30-yard line. Following some short pitches, Hank Brown evaded pressure and rushed 21 yards to cap off the drive with an Iowa touchdown. On the first drive for the Wildcats, backup QB Nicco Marchiol made his first completion of the season on a sideline throw to Hayden Eligon, followed by two first down completions to Griffin Wilde. The ‘Cats, facing a third down on the Iowa 43, took a shot for Luke Dehnicke but fell incomplete and punted to the Iowa 9-yard line. A drive that looked shaky for Iowa, trapped in the midst of its own end zone, almost moved the chains through a defensive pass interference call on third down, but the flag was picked up and the Hawkeyes punted to the Northwestern 41-yard line. However, despite the rather favorable field position, the drive was cut short after only one first down and a third down completion to Dehnicke that fell short of the sticks. Nikola Dugandzic then put on a punting masterclass to pin Iowa back at their own 3-yard line. The tackling struggles continued for the Wildcats, allowing L.J. top.description: Ohio State football lost to Oregon 48-21 at Ohio Stadium on Nov. 7, and the loss probably will cost the Buckeyes a shot at playing in the College Football Playoff or the Big Ten championship game. Combined with last week's defeat at USC, it also marks the first time that OSU has lost back-to-back games since 2011. So how did Ohio State coach Ryan Day explain it? Here are all of his postgame comments. Ryan Day Postgame Press Conference Ohio State vs. Oregon Q: Ryan, you guys obviously went a long stretch there in the second and third quarter where things were in trouble offensively. What was the trouble there with getting Jeremiah [Smith] the ball and getting things going, where things kind of fell apart there? Ryan Day: Well, I think really where the game changed, anyone could see where the game changed, was we lost those two possessions there in the second quarter. They hit the fake punt on us, which is extremely disappointing on our end. Then in that two-minute drill with Luke [Fahey], we decided to be aggressive with it. In hindsight, we probably should have run the ball there and gotten out of the half and into the third quarter. To me, that was a huge turning point in the game. Coming out in the third quarter there, we had the snap go over Luke's head and then weren't able to convert on some of those two fourth-and-2 situations and then the one backed up. We got no rhythm on offense. To me, that put the defense in some tough situations. Q: You've emphasized things all year going into the week, and in your three losses, it kind of seems like your team, coaching staff, or all of it has failed to meet that message. Why do you think that hasn't clicked in those losses and maybe needs to be evaluated? Ryan Day: Yeah, I think we have to evaluate everything. top.title: Zac Taylor shares insight on Shemar Stewart playing time
top.description: The Cincinnati Bengals are gearing up for an early morning primetime showdown with the Atlanta Falcons in Madrid. The Bengals are coming off a stressful overtime win against the Tennessee Titans and are now looking for their sixth win of the season. One storyline that has emerged in the past few weeks is how little former first round pick Shemar Stewart has seen the field. Stewart was the Bengals’ first-round pick in 2025 and has battled injuries and playing time since arriving in Cincinnati. Zac Taylor was recently asked about the Stewart situation, and he shared some insight on everything going on and what he thinks of the former Texas A&M Aggie. “I’ve seen a lot of positive from Shemar. The good part for our team is we have a really deep defensive line group, and that hasn’t been about what Shemar’s been doing, right or wrong. It’s been that we’ve had a really strong group, but now he’s going to get more of an opportunity with Cashius being out, and he’s prepared himself for this moment,” Taylor told reporters this week. “I’m really excited to see him get that opportunity. He’s approached it the right way. He’s had a really good mindset throughout this season. He missed a lot of training camp. That was as big as anything. That was an issue. So, I’m excited to watch Shemar going forward. He’s done everything the right way, and we’re going for him.” Cashius Howell is now on IR, and Cedric Johnson has been dealing with some injury issues, so there could be an opportunity for Stewart to see the field more. Stewart is incredibly athletic, and his skill set could be needed more than ever to bring superstar running back Bijan Robinson to the ground Sunday morning.

top.title: UFC Vegas 124 results: Tatiana Suarez grinds her way to decision win over Virna Jandiroba
top.description: LAS VEGAS, NEVADA - NOVEMBER 07: Tatiana Suarez elbows Virna Jandiroba of Brazil in a strawweight fight during the UFC Fight Night event at Meta APEX on November 07, 2026 in Las Vegas, Nevada. (Photo by Jeff Bottari/Zuffa LLC) Tatiana Suarez wants another shot at gold after her latest win at UFC Vegas 124. While far from the most exciting fight on the card, Suarez used her wrestling to frustrate and control Virna Jandiroba again and again over three rounds. When it was over, the judges scored the fight 30-27, 30-27 and 29-28 with Suarez getting the nod by unanimous decision. “I feel like it was a good matchup,” Suarez said after the win. “She’s excellent on the ground. I’m glad I can experience this with all of you guys. I just wanted to go out there and show everything. I had fun. I had a lot of fun out there. I want that belt. I look forward to the challenge.” Suarez was the first to shoot for a takedown in the battle of grapplers with Jandiroba defending well to stay on her feet. Suarez held onto the single leg while trying to trip the Brazilian to the ground before pushing the action to the fence. Suarez eventually abandoned the takedown to reset in the center of the cage but it wasn’t long before she was grabbing onto the clinch again to use her wrestling. Jandiroba defended well and finally broke free before she exploded forward for a takedown of her own. On the restart in round two, Suarez scored with a good knee to the body before once again diving for the takedown and locking up with Jandiroba against the cage. Jandiroba continued to resist and break free but she just wasn’t doing enough damage on the feet to keep Suarez away from her. Suarez kept trying to employ her wrestling but she just couldn’t drag Jandiroba to the ground. Jandiroba missed with her own takedown with Suarez countering and landing on top but she was mainly holding on for control rather than unleashing much ground and pound. Jandiroba did snatch a late kneebar attempt but time ran out before she could fully extend the submission. With five minutes remaining, Suarez threw some heavy punches but it only took her 90 seconds to dive for another takedown. This time, she got Jandiroba down with Suarez trying to advance her position on the ground. Suarez maintained control as time ticked away until the final horn. It’s going to be hard to deny Suarez another title shot as she continues racking up wins, although she isn’t exactly setting the world on fire with her performances. That said, Suarez matches up well with champion Mackenzie Dern so that could be a matchup to make in 2027.

top.title: Jaland Lowe has 22 points and 8 assists, Georgetown hits 15 3s in 86-74 win over Maryland
top.description: WASHINGTON, DC - NOVEMBER 07: Jaland Lowe #15 of the Georgetown Hoyas goes to basket shot against Bishop Boswell #12 of the Maryland Terrapins in during the college basketball game at Capital One Arena on November 7, 2026 in Washington, DC. (Photo by Mitchell Layton/Getty Images) Mitchell Layton/Getty Images Jaland Lowe made 5 of 8 from 3-point range and finished with 22 points and eight assists Saturday night to help Georgetown beat Maryland 86-74. Elmarko Jackson added 17 points and Kayvon Mulready scored 15 on five 3s for Georgetown (2-0). Vincent Iwuchukwu had 12 points. Lowe and Mulready hit 3-pointers 24 seconds apart that made it 38-26 with 2:38 left in the first half and the Hoyas led by double figures the rest of the way. Pharrel Payne had 28 points and eight assists while shooting 10 of 14 from the field and 8 of 8 from the free-throw line for Maryland (1-1). Freshman Kaden House scored all of his 13 points in the second half. DJ Wagner added 11 points. The Hoyas made 15 3-pointers — the program’s most since in a single game since 2010 — on 30 attempts and shot 52% overall. Mulready hit a 3 that capped a 12-3 opening run in the second half. Georgetown pushed its lead as high as 27 points and led by 22 with 2 minutes left. Maryland, which closed the game on a 19-6 run, made 26 of 63 (41%) from the field and shot just 15% (3 of 20) from behind the arc. Up next Maryland: Hosts No. 9 Virginia on Friday. Georgetown: Hosts Delaware State on Tuesday.

top.title: Tennessee throttles Kentucky 34-6
top.description: KNOXVILLE, TENNESSEE - NOVEMBER 07: Daune Morris #17 of the Tennessee Volunteers runs the ball for a touchdown during the first half of the game against the Kentucky Wildcats at Neyland Stadium on November 07, 2026 in Knoxville, Tennessee. (Photo by Johnnie Izquierdo/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Tennessee Vols did on Saturday to the No. 6 Kentucky Wildcats what the Tennessee Vols do to the Kentucky Wildcats: dominate. Tennessee put a hurting on their border rivals to the north, putting up a 21-point fourth quarter to see a close game finish as a laugher. George MacIntyre was 9/14 passing for 125 yards. DeSean Bishop ran 25 times for 109 yards with two touchdowns. Braylon Staley had four catches for 50 yards. Arion Carter had a whopper of a game with 13 total tackles, two sacks, and four tackles for loss. This was a slow grinder for the first three quarters. The teams traded four punts sandwiched around an interception of Kenny Minchey by Dejuan Lane in the end zone in the first quarter. And then, Daune Morris provided a big spark, ripping off a 66-yard touchdown run to put the Vols up 7-0. The teams traded field goals early in the second quarter, and Tennessee earned a late goal-to-go stop and field goal try to take a 10-6 lead into the locker room. Tennessee started the third quarter with a 10-play, 55-yard drive that ended with a Cooper Ranvier field goal from 39 yards. The teams exchanged punts before Qua Moss forced a fumble near midfield late in the third quarter, and Mariyon Dye picked it up and ran it back 11 yards. Four plays later, Mike Matthews was streaking into the end zone for a 24-yard score and a 20-6 lead. On the following UK drive, on 4th and 1 at midfield, Arion Carter grabbed Minchey and slung him down for a sack and turnover on downs, and with less than 11 minutes left, that was basically it. On the next play, Staley pulled in a 34-yard pass wide open, and Bishop took at five yards for a 27-6 lead. Bishop ran another one in from five yards with a little over a minute left for the game’s final points and a massive exclamation point. Tennessee finished with 389 total yards to Kentucky’s 36 and held a time of possession edge 35:17 to 24:43. Tennessee was penalized seven times for 50 yards; Kentucky was penalized six times for 60 yards.

nigeria.title: U17WWC: You’ve written your names in gold – Tinubu tells Flamingos
nigeria.description: By Johnbosco Agbakwuru President Bola Tinubu has congratulated Nigeria’s Flamingos for making history as the first African team to win the FIFA U-17 Women’s World Cup following their 2-1 victory over Japan in Saturday’s final in Rabat, Morocco. The president, who received the cheering news upon his return from campaign engagements in Akwa Ibom and Rivers States, hailed Nigeria’s maiden triumph as a proud moment for the nation and a landmark achievement for African women’s football. “What wonderful news to return home to! Our young girls have conquered the world and given Nigerians everywhere another reason to celebrate our great country. “To our gallant Flamingos, I say congratulations. You have shown courage, discipline, determination, and the Nigerian spirit of never giving up. “I followed your journey throughout this tournament, and after your semi-final victory, you promised to bring the trophy home. Today, you have kept that promise. You believed in yourselves, fought for one another, and carried our nation’s flag to the very top of the world. “Your victory is an inspiration to millions of young Nigerian girls who dream of achieving greatness. You have shown them that with hard work, opportunity, and determination, they too can reach the highest levels of achievement. “Today, Nigeria celebrates you. You have written your names in gold, and your country is immensely proud of you.” The president particularly applauds Awawu Bashiru and Oluebube Umejiaku, whose goals secured the historic victory, while commending the entire squad for their exceptional teamwork throughout the tournament. He also congratulates the coaching crew, the Nigeria Football Federation, and the National Sports Commission for their contributions to the team’s success. President Tinubu reaffirms his administration’s commitment to investing in grassroots sports development and expanding opportunities for young Nigerians, particularly girls, to discover, nurture, and fulfill their potential. “Congratulations once again, Flamingos. Thank you for making Nigeria proud.” The post U17WWC: You’ve written your names in gold – Tinubu tells Flamingos appeared first on Vanguard News .

nigeria.title: AMERICA IS NOT NIGERIA: Why Trump’s midterm defeat cannot predict Tinubu’s 2027 fortunes
nigeria.description: By Kayode Akinmade The sweeping defeat suffered by President Donald Trump’s Republican Party in the November 3 American midterm elections has predictably provided fresh ammunition for Nigeria’s opposition politicians, who are already attempting to draw parallels between the political fortunes of the American president and those of President Bola Ahmed Tinubu ahead of Nigeria’s 2027 general elections. While the comparison may offer an attractive political talking point, it is, at best, superficial and, at worst, a deliberate attempt to transplant the political circumstances of one country into another. There is no doubt that the Republican defeat represents a significant setback for Trump. Democrats secured control of both chambers of Congress, delivering a powerful electoral rebuke to the Republican administration and signalling widespread dissatisfaction with some of its policies. The result has opened a new chapter in American politics and raised questions about the direction of Trump’s presidency. However, the critical question is whether the circumstances that produced this outcome in the United States are sufficiently comparable to Nigeria’s political and economic realities to justify the conclusion that Tinubu is destined for a similar electoral fate in 2027. The answer is no. America is not Nigeria. Trump is not Tinubu. And the political dynamics of the United States cannot be mechanically imported into Nigeria’s electoral calculations. Indeed, one of the most important factors behind the Republican Party’s defeat was the controversial war involving the United States and Iran, a foreign policy decision that has generated enormous economic, diplomatic and security consequences for the Trump administration. The conflict, which has lasted several months, has heightened concerns about American military involvement abroad, increased pressure on energy markets and contributed to rising fuel prices. For American households already grappling with the cost of living, the war became another source of economic anxiety. Its financial implications, military casualties and uncertain strategic objectives also generated questions about the wisdom of the administration’s foreign policy choices. Iran conflict Significantly, the political consequences were acknowledged by the highest levels of the American government. Trump admitted that the Iran conflict contributed to his party’s electoral difficulties, although he maintained that the military action was necessary. His Vice President, JD Vance, was considerably more direct, declaring that “the reason we lost is the war.” That admission is particularly instructive. nigeria.title: Countdown to 2027: Edo North is for Oshiomhole
nigeria.description: By Allison Abanum Adams Oshiomhole’s first term has been defined by a deliberate strategy of translating legislative power into tangible federal presence for Edo North. As Chairman of the Senate Committee on Interior, he has leveraged his position to facilitate federal employment for constituents and ensure fair representation in federal institutions. His legislative record includes moving over 10 motions and sponsoring many bills. These are not abstract motions; they are institutional investments that will outlast any single political cycle. On the ground, Oshiomhole constituency interventions have reached all wards in Edo North, a coverage rate that speaks to both reach and intentionality. Oshiomhole has moved from delivering roads to delivering accountability, and Edo North have seen the difference in both bricks and budgets. Beyond infrastructure, his engagement with youth leaders and traditional rulers signals a recognition that representation must be relational, not transactional, a point underscored by his refusal to charge constituents for assistance and his warning against extortion in his name. The political consolidation around Oshiomhole 2027 bid reflects a broader strategic calculation within Edo North. Endorsements have since crossed traditional lines: From the market women in Auchi to the Artisan in Iyahmo, down to all the student bodies and community leaders, it is clear that it is no longer a question of whether Edo North is standing for Oshiomhole; it is a question of how loudly Edo North will say so. To the people in the rural areas of Edo North, they have risen from service, unity, and discipline: delivery that touches households, reconciliation that silences internal friction, and grassroots organisation that turns intention into votes. The good people of Edo North on their own are moving ward by ward to get support for Oshiomhole. The plough is heavy; the hands must be steady because the furrow ahead is 2027. The message is clear: no retreat, no sideways glance, no nostalgia for old battles in Edo North. A senatorial district that has seen the light and future must now prove it can cultivate it, row by row, ward by ward, state by state, until the harvest of triumph is achieved. Every leader, every member, every supporter keeps eyes on the furrow, not on the noise. So, let the word go forth: APC is on the plough, and there is no looking back until Oshiomhole is sent back to the Senate in 2027. The task is not to boast of yesterday but to labour for tomorrow with humility, focus, and determination. The harvest belongs to those who keep ploughing. For a senatorial district that has historically oscillated between alignment and agitation, the emerging consensus is that Oshiomhole federal network is an asset too valuable to surrender. Abanum lives in Abuja. The post Countdown to 2027: Edo North is for Oshiomhole appeared first on Vanguard News .

nigeria.title: A Ballot on a Burial Date? Northern Nigeria Confronts the Symbolism of January 16
nigeria.description: By Hassan A Karofi The choice of dates in politics is often presented as a matter of administrative convenience. Yet history teaches us that dates carry powerful symbolism, especially in societies where collective memories of tragedy and triumph remain deeply rooted. As Nigeria prepares for a presidential election scheduled for January 16, 2026, it is important to reflect on what that date means to millions of people, particularly in Northern Nigeria, where January 16 is associated with one of the darkest episodes in the country’s history. The significance of January 16 cannot be understood without revisiting the events of the country’s first military coup. In the early hours of January 15, 1966, a group of young military officers launched Nigeria’s first coup d’état. By the morning of January 16, the consequences of the coup were evident. Several of Nigeria’s most prominent political and military leaders had been assassinated. Among those killed were Sir Ahmadu Bello, the Sardauna of Sokoto and Premier of Northern Nigeria; Sir Abubakar Tafawa Balewa, Nigeria’s first Prime Minister; Brigadier Samuel Ademulegun; Brigadier Zakariya Maimalari; and other senior political and military figures. While leaders from different regions were affected, the perception in the North was that the coup disproportionately targeted Northern political leadership. This perception would profoundly shape political attitudes and inter-ethnic relations for decades. The events following the coup further deepened Northern grievances. entertainment.title: “When Are You Coming Home?” ValueJet Restores Daily Flights to Asaba Ahead of the Festive Season
entertainment.description: Daily Lagos–Asaba and Asaba–Abuja services resume on Friday, 20 November 2026, strengthening regional connectivity and bringing families together for the holidays. Somewhere in Lagos or Abuja right now, a phone is ringing, and the voice on the other end is asking the single question that marks the true beginning of the Nigerian festive season: “When are you coming home?” For thousands of professionals, business owners, and families whose answer is Asaba and the surrounding communities across Delta and Anambra states, ValueJet has delivered timely news. The airline will officially resume daily scheduled flights on its Lagos–Asaba and Asaba–Abuja routes starting Friday, 20 November 2026, just as year-end travel planning reaches peak momentum. The end of the year carries an undeniable emotional pull back to one’s roots. It is the season of growing gift lists, overpacked suitcases, group chats buzzing with reunion itineraries, and the quiet warmth of returning to familiar streets. For many families, December represents the single period in the year when loved ones assemble under one roof. By reintroducing daily non-stop frequency on both routes, ValueJet provides critical operational flexibility for holiday travelers. Whether passengers are heading home early to spend the entire season with family or flying out closer to Christmas Eve after wrapping up the work year, the restored schedule ensures seamless travel options tailored to diverse holiday schedules. “The festive season is fundamentally about people, relationships, and shared moments. At ValueJet, our mission is to ensure that distance never stands in the way of those connections,” said Omololu Majekodunmi , Managing Director of ValueJet. “Restoring our daily services to Asaba reflects our deep commitment to serving the travel needs of our passengers during the most important time of the year. We are proud to offer a reliable, comfortable, and affordable gateway home for families and communities across the region.” The Lagos–Asaba service bridges Nigeria’s commercial capital directly with the vibrant heart of Delta State, facilitating easy access across the South-South and South-East regions. Simultaneously, the Asaba–Abuja route delivers a direct, hassle-free link between the nation’s capital and Asaba, eliminating lengthy road journeys and complex connection itineraries. The resumption complements ValueJet’s rapidly expanding domestic and regional network. Domestically, the airline provides essential air links to key destinations including Port Harcourt, Jos, Owerri, Calabar, Benin, and GWI-Iperu. Beyond Nigeria’s borders, ValueJet continues to extend its reach beyond established destinations like Accra, Banjul, Cotonou, and Malabo with upcoming regional route expansions to Libreville, Monrovia, and Abidjan. entertainment.title: From the Sky to the Earth To You: Earth & Sky by Banke Kuku
entertainment.description: With Earth & Sky , her Spring/Summer 2027 collection, Banke Kuku turns to nature’s most essential cycle: the sky gives rain, the rain feeds the earth, and the earth gives back. Reimagining the water cycle as a circle of life, the collection celebrates the abundance that flows from it. Earth & Sky is built around seven prints in three families. The Sky family is led by the hero print, Bougainvillea Sky, with watercolour bougainvillea, bees, butterflies and birds drifting across a turquoise ground, alongside Dove Sky and Daybreak Sky. The Earth family, Yellow Trumpet and Flower Bud, draws on flowering plants such as Costus spectabilis . The Rain family pairs Raindrop, a glossy, near-photographic print set against the softness of the watercolours, with the Kuku Monogram in fresh colourways. Sky prints are finished with hand-embroidered clouds and raindrops on flowing kaftans and kimono robes. Speaking on the inspiration, Creative Director Banke Kuku shares: “I never start with a sketch. I start with a feeling, and for Earth & Sky, that feeling was abundance. This year I became a mother for the first time, and everywhere I looked, nature was reflecting that same fullness back at me. This is my most personal collection.” A CYCLE OF GIVING BACK In nature, nothing is wasted, and everything returns. Earth & Sky carries that principle as its message: what we take from the earth, we must give back. That principle extends into how Banke Kuku approaches production. The brand maintains a no-waste policy, finding uses for offcuts rather than discarding them, while its seasonless approach allows pieces to remain part of the collection beyond a single season. Banke Kuku also uses digital printing, which consumes less heat and water than conventional printing methods, and continues to reduce its use of man-made fabrics in favour of more conscious material choices. Its commitment to the natural world extends beyond its collections, including its work with the Nigerian Conservation Foundation and its Re-Green Movement, which supports afforestation and the restoration of Nigeria’s natural environment. entertainment.title: FinTribe Finance Fair 2026: Empowers Over 10,000 Women to Build Wealth and Financial Independence
entertainment.description: Over 10,000 women gathered at the Landmark Event Centre, Victoria Island, Lagos, on October 31, 2026, for the fourth edition of FinTribe Finance Fair , a growing movement dedicated to helping African women move from financial awareness to wealth creation and ownership. Themed I CAN and powered by returning lead sponsor Sycamore, the event brought together financial experts, business leaders, entrepreneurs and influential personalities, including Funke Akindele , Omoni Oboli , BamBam , Sola Adesakin and Olufemi Shobanjo , for a day of practical financial education, inspiring conversations and meaningful opportunities. For FinTribe founder Jennifer Awirigwe , popularly known as Financial Jennifer, the fair represents a bigger mission: helping women gain the confidence and resources to take charge of their financial futures. “Financial education is important, but knowledge must eventually become action. We want women to leave Finance Fair knowing that they can save, invest, grow their income, build businesses and take ownership of their financial future,” she shared ahead of the event. Beyond Finance Fair, FinTribe is building a community where women learn about money and put that knowledge into practice . With a presence across 43 countries, the organisation has reached over 20,000 women through financial education, supported more than 5,000 women with capital market training and helped members collectively save and invest millions of dollars. Through its Wealth Builders Academy, savings and investment community, real estate initiatives and recently launched FinTribe App, the organisation continues to create opportunities for women to build healthier financial habits, develop investment confidence and work towards long-term financial independence. At the fair, award-winning filmmaker Omoni Oboli encouraged women to pursue their ambitions without neglecting their wellbeing, reminding them to take things one step at a time, prioritise rest and ask for help when needed. During the Financial Clinic, Sola Adesakin challenged women to become more intentional about their finances, emphasising the importance of earning, budgeting and turning income into real assets. She also introduced the four forces of money: Earnings, Expenses, Engines and Encumbrances. Olufemi Shobanjo of NGX Regulation Limited shared insights into capital market participation, while actress BamBam, marketing strategist and Woof Studios founder Adetutu Laditan, and Mercy Agbeti, popularly known as Christian Money Woman, contributed to conversations about building value, navigating opportunities and growing with purpose. entertainment.title: Inside the Story of Martell’s Afrobeats Limited Edition XO with Davido and Prince Gyasi
entertainment.description: There’s something special about a collaboration that brings together music and visual art, particularly when both creatives have spent years helping African culture reach audiences around the world. For its latest limited edition, Maison Martell has brought together Nigerian music superstar Davido and Ghanaian visual artist Prince Gyasi to create a new expression of its prestigious XO cognac , inspired by the sound, movement and global influence of Afrobeats. The Martell Afrobeats Limited Edition XO will be unveiled in Nigeria on November 6, following the collection’s global launch in New York on October 28. At the heart of the collaboration is Prince Gyasi’s distinctive artistic language. Known for his vibrant colours and imaginative compositions, Gyasi has created an original artwork of Davido that features on the limited-edition bottle and presentation box. The design draws inspiration from the landscapes of West Africa, bringing together Martell’s iconic blue with shades of amber and gold. The blue reflects the rhythmic flow of the ocean, while the golden tones evoke sunlit sands and the warmth of African sunsets. Reimagined through Gyasi’s distinctive, hyper-surreal visual style, these elements create a composition that captures the movement and energy of Afrobeats while celebrating the unity, strength and creative spirit of the continent. For Gyasi, the inspiration goes beyond the visual appeal of the bottle. Growing up in Ghana, his experience of music and its ability to bring people together informed the creative direction of the collaboration. “Growing up in Ghana, I’ve seen firsthand how music brings people together, sparking connection, celebration, and pure joy. As Davido says, ‘We rise by lifting others,’ a reminder that music builds community and lifts us all. I feel a deep pride in Afrobeats, its incredible journey, and the mark it’s making on global music,” Prince Gyasi said. He further explained the thinking behind the colours and composition: “Inspired by the landscapes of West Africa, I blended Martell’s iconic blue with the rhythmic flow of the ocean, golden sands, and waves reimagined in a hyper-surreal style, bringing sound and movement to life. Shades of amber and gold capture the warmth of African sunsets and speak to the continent’s unity, strength, and deep spirit.” The result is an artwork that positions the limited-edition XO as more than a presentation of the cognac itself. It offers a visual interpretation of Afrobeats and recognises the artists and communities whose creativity has helped the genre travel across borders and influence audiences globally. The project also reflects Martell’s five-year relationship with Davido, whose career has developed alongside the international growth of Afrobeats. Bringing Prince Gyasi into the collaboration introduces another creative perspective, connecting music and contemporary African art through a shared celebration of African expression. entertainment.title: UK-based OBIMI Brings Families Together in Lagos to Support Children With Disabilities
entertainment.description: OBIMI CIC is a UK-based community organisation supporting parents and caregivers of children with special educational needs and disabilities (SEND). Its founder, Helen Ewumi , is a qualified social worker and a parent of children with disabilities. Her professional experience and family life both inform OBIMI’s commitment to helping families feel heard, supported and less alone. The Nigeria outreach brought families together in Lagos to share experiences and raise awareness about the importance of understanding disability and challenging stigma. Around 100 families received support through the outreach, including food hampers. Clothing was also shared with families. During the visit, the OBIMI team went to a special school in Lagos and gave pupils school bags and stationery. These practical gifts were offered to support children with their learning and to remind them that they are valued and included. The gathering also created space for families to connect and take part in conversations about disability. OBIMI’s message was clear: every child deserves to belong, and families should be met with understanding, respect and support. For Helen, taking OBIMI’s work to Nigeria was an opportunity to connect with families and communities in Lagos. As a social worker and a parent with lived experience of caring for children with disabilities, she understands how important it is for families to feel listened to and supported. OBIMI CIC is grateful to the families, school staff, volunteers, partners and supporters who helped make the outreach possible. The organisation hopes to continue building connections and raising awareness so that children with disabilities and their families can feel seen, supported and included. A UK-based social worker and parent of children with disabilities, Helen founded OBIMI to support families and challenge disability stigma. entertainment.title: Adaugo Nwankpa: What a Career Transition Taught Me About Starting Over
entertainment.description: One year and two months ago, I took a career pivot. I moved from being a digital media professional writing stories, articles and shaping narratives to becoming an analyst in the energy sector, working across the oil and gas and renewable subsectors. The journey across these two industries that are worlds apart has taught me lessons on starting over You are never really starting from scratch No matter what you are starting over at or what you are getting into, it is important to realise that you are never truly starting from zero. Where ‘zero’ means the state of having nothing: skills, experience, network, intelligence, and others. While it may indeed appear that you do not have the things you consider as being critical to starting over, you actually have what you have: the knowledge, skills and experiences that have shaped your life and marked your journey up to this present moment, and this is invaluable. Also, having a strong knowledge of yourself is also an incredible resource when starting over, as it helps you to discern and differentiate challenges that are due to your personality, and challenges that are due to the circumstance of starting over. Your ‘Next Best Move’ is hidden within your network When we think of network, it is easy to limit it to close friends, relatives or even acquaintances. This is quite a restrictive and limiting view of the concept of network. Your network also includes ‘strangers’ and your internet community. In my case, I knew of the opportunity in the energy sector through a friend whom I had met on Instagram. It gets more interesting. By the time I was preparing for my first interview, I knew that I had zero knowledge about the current state of the sector. Thanks again to Instagram, I reached out to someone I followed who I knew worked in the sector, and she offered a free virtual coffee chat. I went into the interview more confident in what value I could offer and what mattered for such a role. Transferable skills are invaluable Prior to my career pivot, my only exposure to the energy sector aside from buying fuel and gas was a seminar paper I had written in my final year investigating annual shifts in fuel pump prices. However, I audited my skills and qualifications and noted that I also had highly transferable skills. I had communication, business development and a good knowledge and expertise in using Canva. For you, it could be international exposure, multiple languages or something else you think is insignificant. No matter what you are starting over at, you have something that can be transferred from where you were to where you are or where you want to be. Adopt a growth mindset In today’s world, flexibility, adaptability and agility are your currencies for greatness. entertainment.title: Loving Itohan: Come for the Love Story, Stay for Everything Loving Itohan Says About Grief and Family
entertainment.description: Nancy Isime ‘s first film as executive producer, from GREOH Studios, is a beautifully shot story about the love that holds a family together when life falls apart. Some films you watch. Others stay with you. Loving Itohan is the second kind. It opens like the love story you think you already know: a radiant bride, an Edo wedding, coral beads and gold everywhere. You settle in for romance. Then, slowly, the film shows you its heart, and it is so much bigger than a love story. At its centre is Itohan, played by Nancy Isime, a woman whose world is shaken by loss and by truths she never saw coming. What follows is a story about grief, the quiet kind that stays in a home long after the visitors have gone. It is about family, the people who hold us up and sometimes weigh us down. And it is about love that has to keep choosing to stay, even when it hurts. You will see yourself in it. In the person trying to hold everyone together. In the things left unsaid at the dinner table. In the slow, uneven way healing actually happens. A film that looks as good as it feels The cinematography deserves its own round of applause. Every frame feels deliberate, from the rich reds and golds of Edo tradition to the close, quiet moments where a single look says everything. The camera knows when to celebrate and when to simply sit with a character in her pain. This is a film made for the big screen. There is a reason it all feels so assured. Loving Itohan is from GREOH Studios , and Jade studio has never been afraid to go big, with daring, genre-bending stories like Gangs of Lagos. This time, GREOH goes deep instead, trading spectacle for the messy, tender feelings we all carry. True to form, it also hands the director’s chair to a fresh talent, Orobosa Ikponmwen , the latest in a line of new directors the studio has backed, from Kayode Kasum to Loukman Ali. And for Nancy Isime, this is her very first project as an executive producer. You can feel how much of herself she has poured into it, in front of the camera and behind it. Alongside her, Uzor Arukwe, Martha Ehinome Orhiere, Dorathy Bachor, Grace Dein Coker, Chioma Nwosu, Florence Sunday and newcomer Obehi Aburime bring the family to life. Don’t judge it by the trailer If the trailer has you thinking you know where this is going, trust us, you don’t. Go with someone you love. Bring tissues. And maybe call your mum afterwards. Loving Itohan is in cinemas nationwide from 6 November 2026. entertainment.title: Africa Comedy Live Brings Its Platform to Africa, Opening With an Invitation-Only Founding Gathering in Lagos
entertainment.description: Africa Comedy Live (ACL), the platform connecting African comedians, content creators and audiences across the continent and the diaspora, today announces its arrival in Africa with an invitation-only founding gathering, A Salute to Nollywood, to be held on Friday, 13 November 2026 at TRIB3 , Victoria Island, Lagos. The evening marks two milestones at once: the introduction of the Africa Comedy Live platform to the African market, and a formal salute to the comedians and storytellers whose work built the audience that African comedy now commands. Africa Comedy Live has been presenting African comedy live in the United States since 2019, with artists including Kenny Blaq , Helen Paul , Real Warri Pikin and David Operah . The platform, live at www.africacomedylive.com, is another channel, not a replacement for the ones creators already use. It allows creators to keep the audiences they have already built, earn more, and expand opportunities across continents, while giving viewers across Africa and the diaspora a single place to discover the comedians and creators worth following. A Salute to Nollywood brings together comedians, entertainment professionals, media and prospective partners for an evening built around three things: an introduction to the platform through a live demonstration, a celebration of African comedy, and a salute to the generation of performers whose influence continues to shape new talent. “Africa’s comedy has never lacked talent. What it has lacked is a stage that belongs to it,” said Carrie Crawford, Founder of Africa Comedy Live. “For seven years we have put African comedians in front of live audiences in the United States. Now we are bringing that home. Africa Comedy Live is that permanent stage, and Lagos is where it begins,” He added. The gathering is by invitation only and is not open to public attendance. For comedy lovers, the evening is an introduction to the platform and a way to follow the journey. For creators, it is an opportunity to express interest in joining the community. For brands and partners, it is a chance to explore ways to support African comedy’s next chapter. ABOUT AFRICA COMEDY LIVE Africa Comedy Live is a web platform connecting African comedians, content creators and brands across the continent and the diaspora. entertainment.title: Dayo Akinbode: What Travelling to Cuba Taught Me About Money
entertainment.description: I went to Cuba for the salsa, the cigars, the rum and those gorgeous vintage cars. I never imagined that, somewhere between admiring the colourful streets and enjoying the Caribbean sunshine, I would receive an unexpected lesson in money management. Looking back, I can laugh about my experience. But at the time, discovering how much I might have been overpaying left me wondering how much my ignorance had already cost me. Cuba had a way of making me feel as though I had stepped into a film. Imagine standing in a sun-drenched plaza, a Cuban cigar in your hand, the warm Caribbean breeze brushing against your skin, and music floating through the air. Around you, buildings painted in faded yellows, dusty pinks and weathered blues stand proudly, their grand colonial facades and ornate balconies carrying stories from another century. Then comes the rumble of an engine. You turn to see a cherry-red vintage car gliding past, followed by a bubblegum-pink beauty that seems to have driven straight out of the 1950s. Everywhere you look, vibrant colours, rich history and lively movement bring the streets to life And the cars! Oh, the cars! Later, I would find myself riding in a neon-green convertible along the coast, the wind whipping through my hair as the blue Caribbean Sea stretched beside me. I felt wonderfully alive. Cuba was giving me everything I had hoped for: beauty, music, history and the thrill of discovering somewhere different. I was so captivated by everything that I paid little attention to the money in my purse. I visited Cuba in 2019, when the country had two official currencies: the Cuban convertible peso, known as the CUC, and the Cuban peso, known as the CUP. To an unsuspecting tourist like me, this arrangement was a recipe for confusion. I was carrying CUC notes, commonly used by visitors because that is what the banks give you in exchange for your USD notes. The CUC notes looked different from the CUP notes I would later encounter. CUC notes featured monuments, while CUP notes carried the faces of Cuban national heroes, including José Martí and Camilo Cienfuegos. But at the time, I barely noticed the distinction. Money was money, or so I thought. Whenever I needed to pay for something, I reached into my purse, brought out my CUC notes and settled the bill. I was enjoying my holiday and had no reason to suspect my wallet was quietly making it more expensive than necessary. Then, one time, I was given change in a currency different from the familiar CUC. I looked at the notes in my hand and immediately felt that something was wrong. These were not the notes I was accustomed to using. I did not recognise them, and I was not about to walk away with money I did not understand. So, I rejected the change. Imagine my surprise when the cashier and another customer explained to me that the notes were perfectly valid Cuban money! That was when I got my crash course in Cuban economics. sports.title: Knicks put Karl-Anthony Towns trade on the table as $276 million extension talks stall
sports.description: Photo by Caleb Bowlin/Getty Images The New York Knicks have reportedly put a potential Karl-Anthony Towns trade on the table as negotiations over a lucrative contract extension continue to stall. Towns is eligible to sign a four-year extension worth approximately $276 million, but the Knicks are facing financial restrictions under an alleged mandate from owner James Dolan to avoid entering the second luxury tax apron. The 30-year-old still has two years remaining on his current contract, although the final season is a player option that could allow him to become an unrestricted free agent in 2027. New York Knicks could consider trading Karl-Anthony Towns if extension talks fail According to Sean Deveney of Heavy on Sports , New York has discussed the possibility of trading Towns if he decides his future lies away from the franchise. Deveney explained that the Knicks have made the option clear to the centre as both sides continue to work towards an agreement. “The Knicks would be crazy to trade Towns at this point, but then, the Knicks are crazy not to have found common ground on an extension before the season started,” Deveney wrote. “So, we can’t rule out a deal if it looks like Towns will seriously weigh leaving in the summer of 2027. The Knicks have put that option on the table for him, and he will have suitors if nothing changes between now and June 30.” However, the financial gap between the two sides remains significant. According to Stefan Bondy of The New York Post , Towns turned down a four-year offer worth approximately $200 million during the summer. That figure was around $77 million below the maximum extension available to him and would also have represented a pay cut from his current $57 million salary. The Knicks may also have to consider the contracts of Josh Hart and Jalen Brunson, who are both eligible for extensions at different points. Towns’ expectations could also have been influenced by Jalen Duren’s new four-year, $200 million extension with the Detroit Pistons. An anonymous executive told SNY’s Ian Begley that New York would likely need to offer Towns more than Duren received, given his experience and standing in the league. With Towns potentially able to test free agency in 2027, the Knicks face an important decision over whether to meet his financial demands or explore a trade before his contract situation becomes more complicated. Providence did enough to make life difficult on Big Ten contender Nebraska but couldn’t make life easy on itself in a 67-58 defeat Saturday night in the Hall of Fame Tip-Off. “What an amazing crowd. But I can tell you this: we will be.” Nebraska withstood a burst of energy from the Friars and their crowd in the opening minutes. Both teams struggled to score for much of the first half, but the Cornhuskers slowly started to exert their will, then delivered a 9-0 run to jump in front by 11. Providence made a late charge before halftime and trailed by five at the break. The uphill battle included foul trouble for projected standout Miles Byrd, who sat much of the first half with two, then picked up two more in the opening minutes of the second half. The Friars made a move to get within three points with 13:31 left, but the Huskers rolled from there, out-scoring Providence 22-9 over the next 11 minutes. Providence continued to find mixed results at Mohegan Sun Arena despite the proximity to campus, falling to 5-7 all-time. Here are three takeaways from the matchup. One storyline that has emerged in the past few weeks is how little former first round pick Shemar Stewart has seen the field. Stewart was the Bengals’ first-round pick in 2025 and has battled injuries and playing time since arriving in Cincinnati. Zac Taylor was recently asked about the Stewart situation, and he shared some insight on everything going on and what he thinks of the former Texas A&M Aggie. “I’ve seen a lot of positive from Shemar. The good part for our team is we have a really deep defensive line group, and that hasn’t been about what Shemar’s been doing, right or wrong. It’s been that we’ve had a really strong group, but now he’s going to get more of an opportunity with Cashius being out, and he’s prepared himself for this moment,” Taylor told reporters this week. “I’m really excited to see him get that opportunity. He’s approached it the right way. He’s had a really good mindset throughout this season. He missed a lot of training camp. That was as big as anything. That was an issue. So, I’m excited to watch Shemar going forward. He’s done everything the right way, and we’re going for him.” Cashius Howell is now on IR, and Cedric Johnson has been dealing with some injury issues, so there could be an opportunity for Stewart to see the field more. Stewart is incredibly athletic, and his skill set could be needed more than ever to bring superstar running back Bijan Robinson to the ground Sunday morning.

sports.title: UFC Vegas 124 results: Tatiana Suarez grinds her way to decision win over Virna Jandiroba
sports.description: LAS VEGAS, NEVADA - NOVEMBER 07: Tatiana Suarez elbows Virna Jandiroba of Brazil in a strawweight fight during the UFC Fight Night event at Meta APEX on November 07, 2026 in Las Vegas, Nevada. (Photo by Jeff Bottari/Zuffa LLC) Tatiana Suarez wants another shot at gold after her latest win at UFC Vegas 124. While far from the most exciting fight on the card, Suarez used her wrestling to frustrate and control Virna Jandiroba again and again over three rounds. When it was over, the judges scored the fight 30-27, 30-27 and 29-28 with Suarez getting the nod by unanimous decision. “I feel like it was a good matchup,” Suarez said after the win. “She’s excellent on the ground. I’m glad I can experience this with all of you guys. I just wanted to go out there and show everything. I had fun. I had a lot of fun out there. I want that belt. I look forward to the challenge.” Suarez was the first to shoot for a takedown in the battle of grapplers with Jandiroba defending well to stay on her feet. Suarez held onto the single leg while trying to trip the Brazilian to the ground before pushing the action to the fence. Suarez eventually abandoned the takedown to reset in the center of the cage but it wasn’t long before she was grabbing onto the clinch again to use her wrestling. Jandiroba defended well and finally broke free before she exploded forward for a takedown of her own. On the restart in round two, Suarez scored with a good knee to the body before once again diving for the takedown and locking up with Jandiroba against the cage. Jandiroba continued to resist and break free but she just wasn’t doing enough damage on the feet to keep Suarez away from her. Suarez kept trying to employ her wrestling but she just couldn’t drag Jandiroba to the ground. Jandiroba missed with her own takedown with Suarez countering and landing on top but she was mainly holding on for control rather than unleashing much ground and pound. Jandiroba did snatch a late kneebar attempt but time ran out before she could fully extend the submission. With five minutes remaining, Suarez threw some heavy punches but it only took her 90 seconds to dive for another takedown. This time, she got Jandiroba down with Suarez trying to advance her position on the ground. Suarez maintained control as time ticked away until the final horn. It’s going to be hard to deny Suarez another title shot as she continues racking up wins, although she isn’t exactly setting the world on fire with her performances. That said, Suarez matches up well with champion Mackenzie Dern so that could be a matchup to make in 2027.

sports.title: Jaland Lowe has 22 points and 8 assists, Georgetown hits 15 3s in 86-74 win over Maryland
sports.description: WASHINGTON, DC - NOVEMBER 07: Jaland Lowe #15 of the Georgetown Hoyas goes to basket shot against Bishop Boswell #12 of the Maryland Terrapins in during the college basketball game at Capital One Arena on November 7, 2026 in Washington, DC. (Photo by Mitchell Layton/Getty Images) Mitchell Layton/Getty Images Jaland Lowe made 5 of 8 from 3-point range and finished with 22 points and eight assists Saturday night to help Georgetown beat Maryland 86-74. Elmarko Jackson added 17 points and Kayvon Mulready scored 15 on five 3s for Georgetown (2-0). Vincent Iwuchukwu had 12 points. Lowe and Mulready hit 3-pointers 24 seconds apart that made it 38-26 with 2:38 left in the first half and the Hoyas led by double figures the rest of the way. Pharrel Payne had 28 points and eight assists while shooting 10 of 14 from the field and 8 of 8 from the free-throw line for Maryland (1-1). Freshman Kaden House scored all of his 13 points in the second half. DJ Wagner added 11 points. The Hoyas made 15 3-pointers — the program’s most since in a single game since 2010 — on 30 attempts and shot 52% overall. Mulready hit a 3 that capped a 12-3 opening run in the second half. Georgetown pushed its lead as high as 27 points and led by 22 with 2 minutes left. Maryland, which closed the game on a 19-6 run, made 26 of 63 (41%) from the field and shot just 15% (3 of 20) from behind the arc. Up next Maryland: Hosts No. 9 Virginia on Friday. Georgetown: Hosts Delaware State on Tuesday.

sports.title: Tennessee throttles Kentucky 34-6
sports.description: KNOXVILLE, TENNESSEE - NOVEMBER 07: Daune Morris #17 of the Tennessee Volunteers runs the ball for a touchdown during the first half of the game against the Kentucky Wildcats at Neyland Stadium on November 07, 2026 in Knoxville, Tennessee. (Photo by Johnnie Izquierdo/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Tennessee Vols did on Saturday to the No. 6 Kentucky Wildcats what the Tennessee Vols do to the Kentucky Wildcats: dominate. Tennessee put a hurting on their border rivals to the north, putting up a 21-point fourth quarter to see a close game finish as a laugher. George MacIntyre was 9/14 passing for 125 yards. DeSean Bishop ran 25 times for 109 yards with two touchdowns. Braylon Staley had four catches for 50 yards. Arion Carter had a whopper of a game with 13 total tackles, two sacks, and four tackles for loss. This was a slow grinder for the first three quarters. The teams traded four punts sandwiched around an interception of Kenny Minchey by Dejuan Lane in the end zone in the first quarter. And then, Daune Morris provided a big spark, ripping off a 66-yard touchdown run to put the Vols up 7-0. The teams traded field goals early in the second quarter, and Tennessee earned a late goal-to-go stop and field goal try to take a 10-6 lead into the locker room. Tennessee started the third quarter with a 10-play, 55-yard drive that ended with a Cooper Ranvier field goal from 39 yards. The teams exchanged punts before Qua Moss forced a fumble near midfield late in the third quarter, and Mariyon Dye picked it up and ran it back 11 yards. Four plays later, Mike Matthews was streaking into the end zone for a 24-yard score and a 20-6 lead. On the following UK drive, on 4th and 1 at midfield, Arion Carter grabbed Minchey and slung him down for a sack and turnover on downs, and with less than 11 minutes left, that was basically it. On the next play, Staley pulled in a 34-yard pass wide open, and Bishop took at five yards for a 27-6 lead. Bishop ran another one in from five yards with a little over a minute left for the game’s final points and a massive exclamation point. Tennessee finished with 389 total yards to Kentucky’s 36 and held a time of possession edge 35:17 to 24:43. Tennessee was penalized seven times for 50 yards; Kentucky was penalized six times for 60 yards.

sports.title: Shai Gilgeous-Alexander, OKC Thunder roll past Washington Wizards
sports.description: The OKC Thunder turned a cold shooting night for Washington into another win. Shai Gilgeous-Alexander finished with 30 points and nine assists as the Thunder defeated the Wizards 114-75 on Saturday at Paycom Center. Jared McCain added 19 points and five rebounds, while Aday Mara contributed 18 points, eight rebounds and three blocks. OKC held Washington to 29% shooting in the first half and won despite missing forward Jaylin Williams, who sat out his third consecutive game with lower back spasms. The Thunder (8-2) visit the Portland Trail Blazers at 10 p.m. CT Tuesday. Here are three takeaways from Saturday’s win: More: Nikola Topic injury update: OKC Thunder guard assigned to G League team Jared McCain, Aday Mara give Thunder a boost So much for that shooting slump. McCain followed Friday’s 21-point performance against Memphis with another efficient outing, scoring 19 points on 8-of-10 shooting and grabbing five rebounds. After struggling in the three games before Friday, McCain has scored 40 points over his past two outings. Mara gave OKC another productive performance, too. He finished with 18 points, eight rebounds and three blocks, continuing his strong start to the season. He even stretched his range to open the fourth quarter, knocking down a 3-pointer. With McCain finding his rhythm and Mara contributing at both ends, Gilgeous-Alexander had plenty of help. Thunder defense makes Wizards work in first half Washington spent much of the first half searching for breathing room. The Thunder disrupted passing lanes and contested shots, holding the Wizards to 29% shooting before halftime. Wizards star Trae Young managed just four points on 1-of-6 shooting with a turnover in the opening half. Washington’s AJ Dybantsa, the No. 1 pick in the 2026 NBA Draft, recovered from a rough start to finish with a team-high 19 points, six rebounds and three assists. But the Wizards couldn’t turn that production into a road victory. Allen Iverson draws ovation from Thunder crowd One of Shai Gilgeous-Alexander’s biggest basketball influences had a courtside seat Saturday. Hall of Fame guard Allen Iverson arrived in the third quarter alongside Gilgeous-Alexander’s father, Vaughn Alexander, and received a loud ovation when he appeared on the video board. science.title: On this day in space! Nov. 7, 1992: NASA launches Mars Global Surveyor, its 1st Mars mission in 20 years at the time, to map the Red Planet like never before
science.description: null On Nov. 7, 1996, NASA launched its Mars Global Surveyor mission. This was the first mission NASA sent to Mars in almost 20 years! The Mars Global Surveyor spacecraft was an orbiter. It transmitted data from NASA's Mars rovers Sojourner , Spirit and Opportunity back to Earth. The spacecraft also did a lot of its own science. It found surface channels on Mars that appeared to have been created by running water. Mars Global Surveyor looked at the south pole of Mars and saw signs of possible climate change. It also saw a mineral called hematite on Mars. Hematite usually forms in water. NASA then sent its Spirit and Opportunity rovers to look for the hematite, and both rovers found it near their landing sites. Mars Global Surveyor survived much longer than expected. But a space maneuver accidentally exposed one of its batteries to the sun, and the spacecraft lost power. It fell silent forever in November 2006 . NASA launches the Mars Global Surveyor to Mars on a Delta II rocket on Nov. 7, 1996. (Image credit: NASA) Why it mattered As the first successful Mars mission since the two Viking launches in 1975, Mars Global Surveyor ushered in a new era of exploration of the Red Planet, not only through its own contributions to orbit-based science, but by serving a relay for surface-based rovers. As such, it became a primary pipeline for multiple concurrent Mars missions. "The [Mars Global Surveyor] mission overhauled scientists' understanding of Mars by studying the entire Martian surface, atmosphere and interior. Major findings included dramatic evidence that water still flows on Mars in short bursts down hillside gullies, and the identification of water-related mineral deposits leading to selection of a Mars rover landing site for a subsequent mission," read a NASA description of the probe. Mars Global Surveyor sent back more than 240,000 images to Earth during its nine active years. Want more space history? science.title: Send your name to Saturn's moon Titan with NASA's upcoming Dragonfly mission
science.description: null We still may be some time away from sending humans to distant reaches of the solar system, but you can send your name to Saturn's moon Titan, which has the ingredients of life on its surface thanks to NASA's Dragonfly mission. Dragonfly is an SUV-sized nuclear-powered rotorcraft that NASA aims to launch towards Titan in 2028. The agency opened a special events page in late October to allow members of the public to put their name on the spacecraft. The names will be put upon a chip on Dragonfly during the spacecraft's assembly, and all names must be submitted before Jan. 15, 2027. The agency says that the mission has no "ordinary itinerary," as Dragonfly aims to between areas miles (or kilometers) apart after arriving on the surface in 2034. "Nearly a billion miles away, an extraordinary destination awaits. Titan has an atmosphere, rivers and lakes, seasons, sweeping dunes and a landscape rich in organic material," NASA officials wrote in the event page. "Upon arrival in 2034, Dragonfly will fly from place to place on this intriguing world to uncover clues about this remarkable moon, and the chemistry that could help us understand the ingredients for life." Dragonfly will be one of just a few flying crafts on another world, with the first being NASA's plucky Ingenuity mini-helicopter that arrived on Mars along with the still-running Perseverance rover in 2021. Ingenuity was only designed to make five flights, but made it to 72 until its blades were damaged during a landing on Jan. 18, 2024. NASA is now planning a SkyFall mission on Mars that would use three helicopters, and which may launch as soon as late 2028 for the Red Planet. Dragonfly, however, is not the first mission to Titan: that would be Huygens , which operated for just a few hours on Jan. 14, 2005 after deploying from the Cassini spacecraft. Huygens was the first lander on an outer solar system world, and measured Titan's atmosphere and took data from the surface. A mosaic image of Saturn's moon Titan composed of images produced by the Cassini spacecraft. (Image credit: NASA/JPL/University of Arizona/University of Idaho) For its part, Cassini flew by Titan more than 100 times before the mission concluded in September 2017 , providing valuable long-term data about the moon from above. Dragonfly aims to show the moon from up close for about 3.3 Earth years. Its destinations will include dunes and a young impact crater called Selk, according to NASA. "Dragonfly is expected to make one flight every one to two Titan days, which is called a Tsol and lasts about 16 Earth days," NASA officials added of the mission . Dragonfly will stop at a variety of geologic sites, where it will collect samples of surface material for analysis inside the rotorcraft by a suite of scientific instruments." science.title: Star Wars is experiencing a golden age of video games
science.description: After a tumultuous start to EA's rebooted Star Wars Battlefront series, in 2021 Lucasfilm and Disney decided to open up the development of new Star Wars games by bringing in different publishers and studios under the Lucasfilm Games banner. Now, over five years on, we can confidently say we're entering a new golden era of amazing Star Wars games . With LucasArts' successor calling the shots and coordinating a multitude of projects set in a galaxy far, far away, even EA's latest efforts like Squadrons and the Jedi series have taken bigger and bolder swings. Now, in 2026, the full potential of the Star Wars universe has become clearer with specific releases squarely aimed at niche audiences. It's become clear that future Star Wars games needn't be expensive endeavors full of familiar faces or concepts. Star Wars Zero Company and Galactic Racer 's restrained scope and confidence have been infectious, and, as it turns out, they're already recognized by all the parties involved as double-A success stories . Now this is podracing! The original Burnout studio, Criterion, would have been an excellent candidate, but instead they were sent to work in the Battlefield mines. Still, someone was interested in the idea, and the end result is glorious. Fast and furious, Star Wars: Galactic Racer ignores recent racing game trends and bets big on arcade-y vibes, uncomplicated controls, and a high skill ceiling that challenges you with extremely high speeds, tight turns, and unexpected interruptions as other drivers try to ruin your day. The not-so-secret sauce, however, was its runs-based structure, which injects the flexibility and replay value of roguelite games into the more traditional arcade racing structure that older gamers are familiar with. "Star Wars but XCOM" should've happened earlier, but we're glad it did this year, and, unsurprisingly, it's a banger. The correct read of their success should be obvious (and so far, it appears the powers that be are seeing it): Let seasoned and fresh developers cook games they're excited about. science.title: 'I think we will prevail': NASA chief Jared Isaacman on Artemis, China and the new moon race (exclusive)
science.description: null NASA Administrator Jared Isaacman is serious about launching "big rockets" to the moon every single year for the agency's Artemis program. And the new space race with China is fueling that ambition. "I feel good. I feel like we are certainly on a more achievable path to the lunar surface today than where we were before," Isaacman told Space.com. We recently sat down with the NASA chief to discuss the state of the Artemis program , and, off the bat, he made it clear that he's confident in the U.S. space program following the success of April's Artemis II mission around the moon. In fact, just prior to our conversation, it was announced that Artemis II commander Reid Wiseman will become the new deputy director of NASA's Jet Propulsion Laboratory. But the road from Artemis II's success to crewed lunar landings and, later, a permanent moon base will take a lot of launches of NASA's Space Launch System (SLS) megarocket, Isaacman stressed. "You know, a lot of people, especially in the space community, start getting [into] if the landers are there or not. I don't really care about that right now. What I care about is that we are launching big rockets no less than once a year," he said. "I think that's imperative for NASA to be doing these deep-space human spaceflight missions right now," Isaacman added. "So, we had a great mission in April of '26. We will launch again in '27." That coming launch will be for Artemis III, a crewed mission to low Earth orbit that will test docking procedures between NASA's Orion capsule and one or both of the Artemis program's private lunar landers — SpaceX's Starship and Blue Origin's Blue Moon. "We need to continue to exercise those muscles," he said, referring to SLS liftoffs. "And, honestly, once a year isn't great, either. I mean, I don't think we're going to get back to the early [space] shuttle days, you know, four missions a year. I don't think we're going to get back to where we were with Apollo, but once a year is the minimum … I would testify that to Congress in this role years down the road. "If NASA is going to be doing deep-space missions, complicated missions, [we should] launch at least once a year and get as much out of it as you can for taking the risk and spending the taxpayer dollars and building towards something greater," Isaacman added. "That's what we're doing with Artemis III, and that's what's going to better prepare us for Artemis IV." science.title: SpaceX launches mystery mission for US Space Force in gorgeous sunset liftoff from California (video, photos)
science.description: null SpaceX just launched a classified mission for the U.S. military. A Falcon 9 rocket lifted off from California's Vandenberg Space Force Base this evening (Nov. 6) at 7:48 p.m. EST (4:48 p.m. local California time; 0048 GMT on Nov. 7), rising into the sky as the sun sank toward the Pacific. The launch kicked off the USSF-432 mission for the U.S. Space Force , which we know little about. Neither SpaceX nor the Space Force told us much about USSF-432 beforehand, and we learned tonight; SpaceX cut its webcast off about 10 minutes into the flight, shortly after the Falcon 9's first stage came back to Earth for a landing. A SpaceX Falcon 9 rocket launches the USSF-432 mission for the U.S. Space Force from Vandenberg Space Force Base on Nov. 6, 2026. (Image credit: SpaceX) That touchdown occurred aboard the SpaceX droneship "Of Course I Still Love You," which was stationed downrange in the Pacific Ocean. It wrapped up the eighth flight for this particular booster, which is designated 1095. The Falcon 9's upper stage, meanwhile, continued carrying its mystery payload skyward. It could be headed to low Earth orbit , outside observers speculate. "It is possibly a batch of classified LEO satellites for the USSF's Space Based Sensing and Targeting (SBST) portfolio based on SpaceX's Starshield satellite bus, based on locations of rocket stage drop zones being exact fits with previous Starlink Group 15 launches," NextSpaceflight.com wrote in a mission description . Starlink is SpaceX's LEO broadband megaconstellation, which consists of more than 11,000 active satellites. Starshield is a similar system designed to provide services to the U.S. military and its allies. Starshield satellites are believed to be based heavily on the Starlink spacecraft bus. Three were operational flights of the company's Falcon Heavy rocket, while the other three were test missions of its next-gen Starship vehicle.
